zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that X is somewhere to the left (or right) of Y, enforce a strict ordering of their house positions (X < Y for left, X > Y for right).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever the clue uses phrasing like “somewhere to the left/right of”, “to the left of”, “to the right of”, without specifying adjacency.
zebralogic.example: Placing X to the right of Y when the clue says X is somewhere left of Y.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., “Bob is the Desert smoothie lover”), treat them as referring to the same entity and propagate that equality across all categories.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly links a specific value of one attribute to a specific value of another attribute.
zebralogic.example: Treating “Bob is the Desert smoothie lover” as unrelated facts instead of linking Bob to the Desert smoothie.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue fixes an attribute to a particular house number, enforce that assignment exactly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues that contain explicit house numbers, such as “the person in the second house” or “Eric lives in house 4”.
zebralogic.example: Leaving Eric’s house unspecified despite the clue “Eric is in house 4”.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with no extra text after it, to guarantee the verifier extracts the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the end of the response, after all reasoning.
zebralogic.example: Appending commentary after the JSON, causing the verifier to miss the answer.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from being in a particular house, ensure that attribute is not placed there.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues containing phrases like “not in house X”, “cannot be the third house”, etc.
zebralogic.example: Placing the ranch‑style house in house 5 despite the clue “Ranch not in house 5”.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalencePropagation
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B and B = C), deduce the direct equivalence between all linked values.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever there are two or more equivalence clues that share a common value.
zebralogic.example: Failing to infer that the person with the March birthday is also the Victorian‑house owner when given “March birthday = Alice” and “Alice lives in the Victorian house”.

zebralogic.title: ExactAttributeValueMatching
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling and case; never substitute synonyms.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final solution grid.
zebralogic.example: Writing “Mar” instead of the required “mar” for the birthday month.

zebralogic.title: LimitReasoningLength
zebralogic.principle: Keep the reasoning concise enough to stay within the model's token budget, avoiding overly verbose explanations that risk truncation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During the reasoning phase, before outputting the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Providing an excessively long step‑by‑step derivation that exceeds the token limit, causing the answer to be cut off.

zebralogic.title: HouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue specifies a positional relationship with a concrete number of houses between X and Y (including zero for directly adjacent), enforce that the absolute difference in house numbers equals that number plus one.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues containing phrases like “directly left/right of”, “next to”, “there are N houses between”, or “N houses between”.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting “There are two houses between the cat lover and the colonial house” as merely ordering, rather than enforcing a distance of three houses.

zebralogic.title: OverlappingAttributeDisambiguation
zebralogic.principle: When a term appears in multiple attribute categories, use contextual cues (verbs like “has”, “keeps”, “owns”, “loves”) to determine which category the clue refers to, and link attributes across the correct categories.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Any clue that mentions a value that exists in more than one attribute list (e.g., cat, dog, bird, fish).
zebralogic.example: Treating the clue “The cat lover is the person who owns a dog” as linking pet‑cat to pet‑dog instead of linking animal‑cat to pet‑dog.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart'
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the phrase as a simple ordering constraint and forgets the extra house count, leading to off‑by‑one distance errors.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that “N houses between X and Y” means |pos(X) – pos(Y)| = N + 1; enforce the exact numeric distance.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing the verifier to miss the answer
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to generate commentary after the JSON, so the verifier stops parsing at the first non‑JSON token.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Emit the JSON as the very last token of the output and stop generating any further text.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the verifier to truncate
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Overly long reasoning consumes the model's context window, so the tail (including the JSON) gets cut off.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise (e.g., use bullet points, avoid redundant restatements) and monitor token usage.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model focuses on positive constraints and forgets to enforce “not in house X” restrictions.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue contains a negation, add an explicit prohibition rule to the constraint set.

zebralogic.description: Confusing overlapping attribute values across categories
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The same word appears in multiple attribute lists (e.g., cat as a pet and as an animal); the model assumes a single category and links values incorrectly.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Identify the intended category by the surrounding verb (has/keeps/owns/loves) and only link across categories when the clue explicitly indicates a cross‑category relationship.
